Produces a plan@1 artifact where every task includes exact file paths, a brief implementation approach, exact implementation code, the exact tests proving each criterion, a conventional commit message, and covers_criteria linking the task to specific acceptance criteria. spec_file_path and linked_requirement are propagated from the source spec. No TBDs. No "implement as appropriate." Every step is mechanically executable by a developer with zero domain context.
- ranger:audit: Find evidence-backed reachable defects in Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or Go. Refute candidates, group defect families, and verify fixes against current code and the relevant execution boundary.
- scribe:architect: Trigger when `finding-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, or `implementation-result@1` identifies a structural defect class. Produce the smallest `spec@1` that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable through a type, API, boundary, invariant, lint, test, or CI rule.
- scribe:audit-architecture: Trigger when a draft spec@1 needs checking against the workspace's whole-system architecture — not another spec, and not a single signature — before it reaches scribe/gate-spec: "check this spec against our architecture", "does this fit the system", "audit this against the arch model". Given a spec@1, checks it against the persisted arch-model@1 for boundary violations, competing abstractions, and invariant conflicts, building or refreshing the model first if it's absent or stale for the area the spec touches. Returns specific, rewritten fixes on fail, the same standard as scribe/audit-spec but at system scope instead of spec scope.
- scribe:audit-spec: Trigger when the user asks to review a spec's quality: "review this spec", "is this spec complete?", "audit this spec". Given a spec@1, adversarially reviews it for untestable criteria, ambiguous language, missing error cases, scope overlap with other specs, and incomplete sections. Returns a structured issue list with specific rewritten suggested fixes, not generic guidance. Named audit-spec rather than audit because the bare word audit is already ranger's plugin-level skill name (code/bug auditing) — a different domain entirely.
- scribe:correct-spec: Trigger when implementer reports that a spec criterion contradicts what the system actually does: a spec_contradiction status from smith. Given a spec_file_path, the criterion_id of the affected acceptance criterion, and a contradiction report (what the spec says vs. what the system actually does), revises the affected criterion — and any criteria that depend on it — and returns a corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. Use this when implementation reveals the spec itself is wrong, not merely hard to satisfy.
- scribe:draft-spec: Trigger when the user asks to write or draft a spec: "spec this out", "draft a spec", "write a spec for this requirement". Given a requirement@1 and optionally a research-report@1, produces a spec@1 draft with purpose, scope, non_goals, api_surface (if applicable), and acceptance criteria. Every criterion is a testable proposition; error cases carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs anywhere in the document — genuinely unknown items go in non_goals or the reasoning scratchpad instead.
- scribe:gate-spec: Trigger when a spec@1 needs a definitive pass/fail judgment before it enters planning: "gate this spec", "is this spec ready?", "check this spec before we plan it". Default disposition is fail — the spec must earn a pass. Passes only if every acceptance criterion is testable with no vague language, no TBDs remain, error cases are explicitly covered, and scope is narrow enough for one planning cycle. This gate checks the spec on its own terms — whole-system architectural fit is scribe/audit-architecture's job upstream, not re-litigated here. On fail, returns blockers specific enough for scribe/draft-spec to act on without further clarification.
- scribe:spec-drift: Trigger when the user asks whether implemented code still matches its spec, weeks or months after implementation: "check spec drift", "does the code still match this spec?", "has this spec drifted?". Given a spec@1 (via spec_file_path) and a workspace root, reads the spec from disk and the implementation from the workspace, and reports each criterion as covered (implemented and tested), uncovered (no matching implementation), or drifted (implementation exists but diverges from the criterion's contract). This is an on-demand diagnostic, not a blocking gate — scribe/gate-spec is the blocking gate.
- scribe:verify-spec: Trigger when the user asks whether a spec matches its source: "is this grounded?", "does this spec match the requirement?", "check this spec against the requirement". Given a draft spec@1 plus the originating requirement@1 and optional research-report@1, checks whether each acceptance criterion is grounded in the source artifacts. Classifies criteria as supported, unsupported, or overfitted. Collects evidence only — does not produce a pass/fail verdict. Use before implementation, not after — for post-implementation drift, use scribe/spec-drift instead.
- sentinel:gate: Trigger this skill when the user says "verify this", "check this spec", "check this plan", "check this requirement", "check this PR", "is this done?", "review this for completeness", "does this meet the criteria?", "gate this", or "quality check" — also before stage transitions: starting implementation from a spec, shipping from an implementation, opening a PR from a branch. Applies to any stage artifact: requirements, specs, plans, implementations, PRs. Do not activate for general Q&A, code explanation, or exploratory work with no artifact boundary being crossed. The gate either clears the artifact for the next stage or returns specific, actionable blockers to the producing agent.
- smith:implement: Activate for implementation, implementation tests, or behavior-preserving refactoring. Execute bounded batches with risk-based verification, defect-family review, and an independent scoped verdict. Do not activate for explanation-only requests.
- vanguard:research: Activate when the user says "I need to understand X before deciding", "is there a way to do Y", "what are the options for Z", "research this", "investigate this", "what does the codebase already do for X", "prior art on Y", or "what are the risks of approach Z" — also when the approach for a spec or plan is unclear, when checking what dependencies exist for a feature, or when any design question needs an evidence base before commitment. Investigates the question across internal sources (specs, docs, codebase patterns, manifests) and external sources as needed, then produces a research-report@1 that distinguishes confirmed findings from likely inferences from unverified assumptions, with a falsifiable recommendation and explicit confidence level so a spec writer (scribe) isn't surprised by implementation reality.
- weaver:audit-backlog: Trigger when the user asks about overall backlog health: "what's in the backlog", "audit the backlog", "what requirements are missing coverage". Cross-references all open requirement@1 objects against existing specs and implementation files. Returns per-requirement status (covered, partial, missing, duplicate) with evidence, plus a structured summary — per-status counts and an optional one-clause note, not a prose paragraph. Named audit-backlog rather than bare audit because that word is already ranger's plugin-level skill name (code/bug auditing) — a different domain entirely.
- weaver:capture-need: Trigger when the user describes a raw need in free text: "we need X", "the problem is Y", "users are asking for Z". Converts unstructured text into a structured requirement@1 draft — id, statement, stakeholder, why, done_when — without asking clarifying questions. Fields that cannot be inferred are omitted, not fabricated. out_of_scope is intentionally left empty for weaver/connect-requirement or a human to fill in.
- weaver:clarify-requirement: Trigger when a requirement@1 draft from weaver/capture-need has gaps to close before a spec can be written: "is this requirement complete?", "what's missing from this requirement". Given a requirement@1, evaluates gaps in priority order — testability of done_when, specificity of stakeholder, explicitness of out_of_scope — and either asks one focused question or returns the completed requirement with out_of_scope populated. One question per invocation, never a list.
- weaver:connect-requirement: Trigger when the user asks whether a specific requirement already exists or relates to other work: "is this already captured?", "does this overlap with an existing requirement?", "what does this relate to?". Given one requirement@1 (or a small named set), searches the workspace for related specs and implementation files, and checks for duplicate or overlapping requirements. Returns coverage status and duplicate_of references scoped to just the requirement(s) given — not a full backlog sweep.
- weaver:prioritize-backlog: Trigger when the user asks what to work on first from a set of requirements: "what should we prioritize", "rank the backlog", "what's most urgent". Given a list of requirement@1 drafts, ranks them by impact, urgency, and dependency order — a requirement another depends on ranks above the one depending on it, even if its own impact/urgency score is lower. === callisto.toml ===
# callisto configuration
#
# Mirrors ~/projects/michi's proven callisto.toml shape — the closest
# existing reference for a Rust-crates + NAPI-binding + npm-wrapper
# monorepo. One structural difference from michi: michi's NAPI crate and
# its npm wrapper share a single directory (packages/michi-node/, holding
# both Cargo.toml and package.json), whereas this repo splits them across
# crates/binding (the cdylib) and packages/napi (the npm wrapper) — expressed
# as two separate [[package]] entries joined by a [[fixed-group]] below, the
# same mechanism michi uses for its own crate+wrapper pair.
#
# `[[package]] match` is a PACKAGE NAME (bare, or "<ecosystem>/<name>"
# ecosystem-qualified — one of cargo/npm/pypi/go/maven/nuget/deno/jsr),
# never a directory path — confirmed against callisto-model's PackageId::parse
# and callisto-graph's own test suite (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/
# resolve.rs, tests/per_package_config_test.rs). A directory-path `match`
# (e.g. "crates/core") parses to a literal bare name that no real package is
# ever named, so the rule silently matches nothing — verified empirically:
# an earlier draft of this file used directory paths for every [[package]]
# entry and callisto plan-publish still listed crates/binding for a cratesIo
# publish despite publish-to = [] below, because that override was never
# actually being applied. michi's own callisto.toml has this same mistake
# (match = "packages/michi-node", match = "."), which is presumably why it
# went unnoticed there too — its manifest-derived defaults happen to already
# match what it wants.
#
# Pinned to callisto 0.8.0 (GitHub Release `callisto@0.8.0`, commit
# c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393). .github/workflows/release.yml
# pins both callisto actions to that commit and installs the attested
# prebuilt CLI with `verification: require`.
#
# 0.8 split releasing into two authority boundaries: callisto-action only
# creates or updates the `callisto/version-packages` PR — its former
# `publish` input no longer exists — and publication runs from the merged
# release commit through `callisto release plan` → `callisto release execute`
# in this repo's own durable workflow. That path reads the `publish-to`
# overrides below as authority, unlike the legacy `callisto plan-publish`
# command this file was originally written against.
#
# 0.8 also adds a `[release]` section for product binary assets, deliberately
# unused here: its `artifact-targets` are validated against callisto's own
# hardcoded (target, asset-name) table (`PRODUCT_ARTIFACT_TARGETS`), so no
# other workspace can declare it. With no `[release]` section the derived
# intent carries no artifact slots, which release.yml asserts before
# executing.
#
# No .moon/workspace.yml changes are needed: the moon WASM extension
# (crates/callisto-moon) only implements read-only `status`/`plan-publish`
# reporting subcommands — no `publish`/`tag`/apply path exists through it.
# setup-callisto puts the `callisto` binary on $GITHUB_PATH directly; moon is
# installed alongside it as a toolchain dependency, not as callisto's host.

# Group members and changeset frontmatter resolve bare names through
# callisto's identity index, which errors on an ambiguous name rather than
# guessing. The private root package.json is therefore named
# `oxc-react-docgen-workspace`, not `oxc-react-docgen`: sharing the CLI
# crate's name made every `oxc-react-docgen: patch` changeset ambiguous
# across cargo and npm. The fixed-group members below stay ecosystem-
# qualified anyway, since that is cheap insurance against the same collision.

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

# Rust library crate — published to crates.io, no npm counterpart. Consumed
# via path dependency by both crates/cli and crates/binding.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen-core"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Rust CLI crate — published to crates.io. packages/cli wraps its compiled
# per-platform binaries for npm distribution; kept in lockstep below.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# npm CLI wrapper — distributes crates/cli's compiled binaries.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/cli"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# NAPI binding crate (cdylib) — not published to crates.io independently (no
# real-world use case for `cargo add`ing an FFI shim on its own). Callisto
# still tracks/bumps its version to stay in lockstep with its npm wrapper via
# the fixed-group below, but is excluded from the crates.io publish plan.
#
# Under 0.8's release path this override is authoritative: intent derivation
# builds registry-publish operations (and the tag that depends on them)
# straight from `publish-to`, so an empty list yields neither a crates.io
# publish nor a tag for this crate. crates/binding/Cargo.toml's own
# `publish = false` remains the second gate — callisto-manifests'
# is_publishable() still treats a missing `publish` key as true, which is
# what the legacy `callisto plan-publish` command reads.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen-napi"
publish-to = []
release-trigger = "changeset"

# npm NAPI wrapper — distributes crates/binding's compiled .node binaries.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/napi"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Vite plugin — standalone npm package, no Rust counterpart.
[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Keep the NAPI binding crate and its npm wrapper versioned in lockstep —
# the npm package is meaningless without a matching binding build.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "napi-and-binding"
members = ["cargo/oxc-react-docgen-napi", "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/napi"]

# Keep the CLI crate and its npm wrapper versioned in lockstep — the npm
# package just redistributes this crate's compiled binaries.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "cli-and-npm-wrapper"
members = ["cargo/oxc-react-docgen", "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/cli"]
=== release.yml ===
name: Release & Publish

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged Callisto release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

# Least privilege at workflow scope. Every job opts into exactly what it needs,

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.

- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.

**#136** feat(init)! first-run setup — `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/init.rs`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs`. `init` now detects facts and asks only intent (versioning, binary shipping); refuses to run if `callisto.toml` exists (`ensure_uninitialized`, PR136 diff L2148-2153, `GraphError::InitAlreadyInitialized`). Not directly actionable for us since we already have callisto.toml — but it means **`init --workflow`/`--yes` from #138/#139 cannot run against this repo without deleting callisto.toml first** (no bypass flag found in #138/#139 diffs).

**#137** feat(status)! `status --check` replaces `validate` — `.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`, `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/{status,validate}.rs`. `callisto validate` removed entirely; moon extension's `validate` dispatch returns `E_REMOVED`. We don't currently invoke `callisto validate` or the `callisto-validate` action anywhere in `.github/` (grep confirmed) — no action needed, just don't add `validate` calls going forward.

**#138** feat(init) generate simple release workflow; `callisto-action` `mode` input — `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`. Adds `mode: version-pr|release` (default `version-pr`, backward compatible with our current usage). Internally, `setup-callisto`'s steps are now called directly via `github.action_path` instead of `uses: $/...` (pure internal refactor, no input/output change for us). Only generates a 2-job workflow for **non-build-matrix** workspaces — irrelevant to us since we have napi platform packages.

**#139** feat(init) generate matrix workflow — `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs`, `commands/init.rs`. Adds a 4-job (`version-pr`/`plan`/`build`/`execute`) generator for workspaces with napi platform packages or `[[release.artifact]]` cargo binaries. `callisto matrix` output gains a `kind: cargo` entry per `[[release.artifact]]`.

## 2. Exact breaking changes (old → new)
- `callisto validate` → removed; use `callisto status --check` (exit 0/1 on errors only) + `callisto release --dry-run`. Pending-changeset detection: `.pending` count now comes from `status --format json`, not validate's exit code. (not used by us today)
- `init` reconcile-on-existing-config → `init` now hard-errors (`InitAlreadyInitialized`) if `callisto.toml` exists; `[init]` table in toml still loads but is ignored.
- `init --yes` alone → now requires `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`.
- Generated release workflow path: `.github/workflows/release.yml` → **`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`** — hardcoded as `callisto_model::RELEASE_COORDINATOR_WORKFLOW_PATH`; `release execute`'s `attest-build-provenance` signer-workflow check is bound to this exact path (PR139 diff L1633, L2004 revision_note). Our repo's hand-written file is still named `release.yml` — doesn't break today (no artifact attestation in use) but blocks future adoption of build-matrix attestation without a rename.
- `callisto-action`: `publish`/`create_github_release` inputs stay ignored (already true pre-#138); `mode` is additive, default unchanged.

## 3. Would the generated workflow build our napi/CLI binaries?

**napi (`packages/napi` + `crates/binding`): partially, with manual edits required.**
- Matches the "napi platform packages" build-matrix shape (`napi.targets` in `packages/napi/package.json`) — `callisto matrix` picks it up (PR139 `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs` L1435+).
- Generated `build` job runs `napi build --platform --release --target $TRIPLE` with `cd "${PACKAGE_DIR:-.}"` — **no `--manifest-path`** (PR139 diff L748-754). Since our crate (`crates/binding`) and npm wrapper (`packages/napi`) are in different directories — the exact case explicitly called out in the PR's own changeset — this step **will fail as generated**; the changeset itself says (`docs/06-publishing.md` L1643, PR139 diff): "napi build runs in the napi package's directory... add `--manifest-path` to that step" — manual patch required.
- `execute` job requires `*.node` gitignored (PR139 diff L1644) — must verify `packages/napi/.gitignore`.

**CLI (`packages/cli` per-platform `optionalDependencies`, e.g. `@oxc-react-docgen/cli-darwin-arm64`): NOT covered at all.**
- The matrix's only cargo-binary source is `[[release.artifact]]` in `[release]` config (PR139 `add_release_artifact_groups`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs` L1433-1483), and our `callisto.toml` deliberately has no `[release]` section (per its own header comment).
- `[[release.artifact]]` binaries are published **as GitHub Release tarball/zip assets** (`docs/06-publishing.md`, PR139 diff L1654: "binary assets are published to the GitHub Release"), attested via `actions/attest-build-provenance` (PR139 diff L798-801) — a fundamentally different distribution model than our npm-optionalDependencies-per-platform scheme for `@oxc-react-docgen/cli-*`.
- Callisto has no concept of "cargo binary shipped as per-platform npm package" outside the napi convention. To get callisto to build our CLI binaries we'd have to re-architect distribution to GH Release assets, or keep hand-writing that half ourselves.

**Config needed from us if adopting the generated workflow:** delete/bypass existing `callisto.toml` to let `init` run (currently blocked, see #2); rename our workflow to `callisto-release.yml`; add `--manifest-path crates/binding/Cargo.toml` to the generated napi build step by hand; gitignore `*.node`; decide CLI binary distribution stays hand-rolled (generated workflow won't touch it).
